text:
maria: heads up 2d small but nasty thing: Next.js middleware on edge started throwing during auth when I upgraded the SDK. Error shows `ReferenceError: require is not defined` then after switching imports `TypeError: crypto.subtle is undefined`.
kevin: oh no. which import path did you use initially?
sam: common pitfall: CJS require inside code that gets bundled for edge. paste the line.
maria: had `const { createClient } = require('@redwood/inference')` inside middleware.ts. fixed to `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` but still hit the crypto problem.
leo: `@redwood/inference` defaults to the node build. for edge/middleware you should import the explicit edge entry `@redwood/inference/edge`.
maria: I tried `/edge` but still saw `crypto.subtle` missing on both `next dev` and our Vercel preview.
kevin: Next's dev server and some edge runtimes differ in WebCrypto exposure. Vercel's runtime usually has `globalThis.crypto.subtle`, but dev may not. Also check your Node version for dev shim.
sam: short-term dev workaround: guard calls to subtle and fallback to a tiny JS sign routine (only for dev). eg: ```ts
const subtle = globalThis.crypto?.subtle ?? undefined;
if (!subtle && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development') { /* use shim */ }
```
maria: I hacked a local adapter `lib/rw-edge.ts` that re-exports `@redwood/inference/edge` and that fixed preview behavior. suggests the bundler was collapsing exports and picking wrong file when imported directly from middleware.
leo: that happens when package `exports` map is ambiguous. We should harden package.json conditional exports and also ship an edge-only entry that asserts web APIs at module init.
kevin: agreed. action items for SDK: 1) ensure distinct exports for node/module/edge, 2) add runtime guards with clear messages (e.g., "Edge build expected web crypto; found none - did you import the node build?"), 3) add Next middleware docs and example.
sam: also add tests that run a small Next build against the example to catch resolver issues. bundlers can be weird with tree-shaking and package conditions.
maria: other gotcha: streaming differences. our middleware used `response.body.getReader()` and that was undefined in one preview region. I added a defensive helper `readableToArrayBuffer(res)` to fallback reliably.
leo: good call. SDK should include tiny helpers: `safeFetch`, `safeGetReader`, and `ensureAbortController` that normalize across edge variants.
kevin: also call out in docs: never `require()` in files that Next might bundle to edge (middleware, app router edge handlers). use explicit edge import.
maria: I like the idea of early runtime checks. a fail-fast error would have saved time.
sam: I'll open a PR: export fixes + init-time asserts in the edge build + docs + a minimal next-middleware sample repo.
leo: deploy-bot created branch `edge-next-import-fixes` and kicked CI.
deploy-bot: branch `edge-next-import-fixes` created; CI queued.
maria: thanks all, the adapter trick and the thread helped me unblock. will revert my adapter once the release lands. :relieved:
